# @zakkster/lite-signal-decorators

VERSION 1.5.0

> Standard-decorators layer over @zakkster/lite-signal, built on the TC39
> decorators proposal (Stage 2.7 since 2026-05; TS 5.x / Babel 2023-11 emit
> unchanged). Turns a plain class into a
> reactive view-model where each instance has a measured per-property cost, a
> single deterministic teardown, and poison-on-dispose safety. ESM-only, zero
> runtime dependencies beyond the peer. The accessor read/write bodies carry one
> slot load + one monomorphic box call -- zero branches, zero allocation.

A `@reactive accessor` becomes a per-instance signal box stored in a unique
symbol slot. A `@derived get` becomes a lazy computed owned by the instance's
anchor. A `@reactiveEffect` method auto-runs as an effect after wiring; a
`@batched` method runs its writes inside one engine batch. `@reactiveHost` is
the one place wiring happens -- its most-derived constructor builds the anchor,
every derived, and every effect exactly once, after all fields initialize.
`defineReactive(Class, spec)` is the buildless twin: the identical wiring with
zero decorator syntax, sharing the SAME core by function identity.
`disposeReactive` cascades that anchor, disposes each signal box, and swaps every
slot for a poison handle, so any later read/write throws a named
`ReactiveDisposedError`.

## Exports (23)

- `reactive` -- `@reactive accessor x = v` (bare) or `@reactive({ equals })`
  (factory). Declares a per-instance signal.
- `derived` -- `@derived get y()` (bare) or `@derived({ equals })` (factory).
  Declares a lazy computed derived from other reactive members.
- `localTo` -- `@localTo(source) accessor x = v` or
  `@localTo(source, { equals? })`. Upstream-keyed resettable local state
  (decisions/0014). `source` is a REQUIRED tracked `(self) => value` fn, called
  inline in the read body (no extra node, PD-54). The read is PURE (never writes
  a box): it calls `source`, compares the value to a per-instance last-seen slot
  via `equals` (default `Object.is`), and returns the local box `.get()` when
  upstream is unchanged, else the upstream value (a changed upstream resets to
  it). A write always overrides -- the write path never compares (PD-56).
  Initial-value unification (0014): with an initializer the member STARTS at that
  value and resets on the first upstream move (@trackedReset flavor); with NO
  initializer the initial is the source evaluated once at wiring and the member
  FOLLOWS upstream from the first read (@localCopy flavor) -- one decorator, both
  semantics, selected by the natural syntax. `equals` governs the UPSTREAM
  compare ONLY. A throwing source propagates from the read, mutating nothing
  (fail closed). ABA contract (shipped, honest, never softened): no public epoch
  exists (NodeDescriptor is {id, kind, value}), so the compare is VALUE-based --
  upstream A -> local write X -> upstream B -> upstream back to an equals-A value
  -> the read shows the STALE LOCAL X (the reset needs upstream to change
  relative to the last adoption, not to have moved transitively). tracked-toolbox
  @localCopy has the same property. Storage per member: ONE signal box + ONE
  plain per-instance seen-slot (never reactive); cost delta +1 node, +0 for the
  slot -- the per-instance formula becomes P+L+D+E+1.
- `reactiveEffect` -- `@reactiveEffect m()` (bare) or
  `@reactiveEffect({ scheduler })` (factory). A method that auto-runs as an
  effect once the instance is wired. The auto-effect tracks; the public method is
  a leak-guarded manual entry (a call inside a foreign tracking scope is
  untracked, adding zero stray dependencies -- D-4b). Manual calls are also
  identity-guarded (D-4e): invoking a decorated method on a foreign, primitive,
  null, or cross-class receiver throws a named error instead of running against
  the wrong instance.
- `batched` -- `@batched m()` (bare) or `@batched()` (factory). Runs the method
  body inside one engine batch. Action-grade (one call per user intent), NOT a
  per-frame path: it allocates a thunk + rest-array per call by design, so it is
  excluded from the zero-GC hot-path gates. Buildless callers batch with
  `registry.batch(...)` directly (no `batched` section in the spec).
- `reactiveHost` -- `@reactiveHost` (bare) or `@reactiveHost({ registry })`
  (factory). The single wiring site; wraps the class. A `registry` isolates the
  whole host chain (see the registry law).
- `defineReactive(Class, spec) -> Class'` -- the buildless twin. `spec` is
  `{ signals, deriveds, locals, effects, host }`; it installs the members on
  `Class.prototype` and wraps the class through the same host step. See the
  buildless contract.
- `disposeReactive(vm) -> boolean` -- cascade + poison teardown. Idempotent: a
  second call returns `false` and changes nothing.
- `releaseReactive(vm) -> boolean` -- park a LIVE instance to the engine pool:
  cascade the anchor, dispose each signal box, swap every slot to a per-class
  PARKED handle, keep the prebuilt wiring closures. A parked instance holds ZERO
  engine nodes. `true` on the first release, `false` on park->park (idempotent,
  mirrors double-dispose). Fails closed on a disposed, unwired, frozen, or
  non-reactive value. See the pooled-lifetime contract (decisions/0010, 0011).
- `reinitReactive(vm, initials?) -> vm` -- revive a PARKED instance: rebuild each
  signal box (`initials[key]` wins, else the plan initial), rebuild the anchor +
  deriveds + effects through the SAME prebuilt closures, restore live slots.
  Atomic: any throw mid-reinit routes through disposeCore and lands the instance
  DISPOSED (a failed revival is final). Fails closed on a live, disposed, frozen,
  unwired, or non-reactive value. Two-call lifecycle by design (decisions/0011).
- `boxOf(vm, key) -> SignalBox | ComputedBox` -- the live box behind a member;
  throws with a did-you-mean on an unknown key, `ReactiveDisposedError` after
  dispose.
- `rootOf(vm) -> NodeDescriptor` -- the instance's anchor descriptor; feeds
  `forEachOwned` / lite-devtools. Throws `ReactiveDisposedError` after dispose.
- `forEachReactive(vm, fn, arg) -> count` -- cold value-member walk. Calls
  `fn(key, box, kind, arg)` once per value-bearing member and returns the visit
  count. `kind` is `"signal" | "local" | "derived"`; `@reactiveEffect` and
  `@batched` are EXCLUDED (non-value-bearing -- `boxOf` refuses them). Order is
  PLAN order: signals, then locals, then deriveds, each declaration-ordered and
  ancestor-first (never `Reflect.ownKeys`, so it is stable across reinit). Four
  scalar args, zero descriptor object, and the `arg` pass-through kills the
  caller's closure -- the walk is a gated zero-alloc body. Symbol-keyed members
  are visited (`byKey` is a Map). Fails closed on a non-reactive, unwired,
  parked, or disposed value with the same named errors as `rootOf`.
- `snapshotOf(vm) -> plain object` -- a shallow plain-object copy of every
  value-bearing member (signals + locals + deriveds), keyed by member key.
  Values are read through the ACCESSOR `vm[key]` (NOT `box.get`), so a `@localTo`
  compare-on-read resets honestly and a `@derived` computes on read. The whole
  walk runs under ONE `reg.untrack` thunk when `reg.isTracking()`, so calling it
  inside an effect subscribes to NOTHING. SHALLOW by design: a nested VM is
  copied by reference, not recursed (recursion needs a seen-set + cycle law,
  deferred to a named consumer). Symbol keys are included
  (`Reflect.ownKeys` law). Fails closed on parked/disposed (named
  `ReactiveDisposedError`) and non-reactive values. This export ALLOCATES by
  design (the returned object; ~96 B/op measured) and is reported, never gated --
  the walk under it stays zero-alloc.
- `costOf(Factory) -> { nodes, links, signals, deriveds, effects }` -- the
  measured settled per-instance cost on the class's bound registry (frozen,
  cached). Double-probed: an inconclusive or polluted probe throws, never
  guesses. `nodes` = P+L+D+E+1; `links` = the first-full-read link count. See
  "Introspection & audit".
- `costOfInstance(vm) -> { nodes, links, signals, locals, deriveds, effects }` --
  the LIVE measured cost of one wired instance right now, walked from its own
  graph. The delta from `costOf` IS the feature: `costOf` answers "what will an
  instance of this class cost" (it forces every derived to the constructed
  ceiling), `costOfInstance` answers "what does THIS instance cost right now" --
  an unforced lazy derived or an untaken dynamic branch has formed no links yet,
  so `links` reads BELOW `costOf` for the same shape until the graph is
  exercised; `nodes` matches regardless. Read every derived once and the two
  agree exactly (forced parity === costOf). UNCACHED by design -- a live graph
  mutates, so a cached number would lie; every call re-walks. Allocates its
  frozen result by design (one object per call, ~71 B/op, cold like snapshotOf --
  reported, never gated). Needs no stats() ledger, so it measures instances on
  hand-rolled registries where `costOf` fails closed. Fails closed on a
  disposed/parked instance with a NAMED throw -- a parked vm holds zero nodes and
  a silent `{ nodes: 0 }` is indistinguishable from a bug -- and on unwired,
  no-plan, or prewired-member values. See "Introspection & audit".
- `capacityFor(inventory, { headroom }?) -> RegistryConfig` -- size a
  `createRegistry` config from `[Factory, count]` pairs. Nodes exact, links x
  `headroom` (default 1). Fail-closed inventory validation.
- `createFleet(inventory, bind, opts?) -> Fleet` -- the flagship-audience fleet
  helper over the shipped primitives (`capacityFor` + `createRegistry` +
  park/reinit; decisions/0013 criterion (d)). COLD construction sizes a registry
  from `inventory`, builds it, hands it to `bind(registry)` (the caller binds its
  decorated class to that registry and returns it -- the helper never wraps or
  redefines the class), then EAGER-constructs and PARKS one member per inventory
  unit. Returns a handle `{ registry, Class, capacity, acquire(initials?),
  release(vm), at(i), size(), stats(), dispose() }`. Import in the exports block:
  `import { createFleet } from "@zakkster/lite-signal-decorators"`. LAWS: eager
  prefill is done at construction -- `acquire` never constructs, it pops a
  free-list and `reinitReactive`s a parked member (`initials` override the reset
  values); `release` validates a per-fleet slot stamp and `releaseReactive`s the
  member back to the pool. Both hot bodies allocate ZERO (a slot array + an
  `Int32Array` free-list + a per-vm symbol slot stamp -- never a WeakMap). SIX
  named fail-closed misuses: `acquire` at capacity throws `FleetExhaustedError`
  (pre-checked; the registry's own `CapacityError` is unreachable, all N are
  prealloc'd); `release` of a foreign vm throws `FleetForeignMemberError` (the
  slot stamp is the check); a double release throws `FleetDoubleReleaseError`;
  any call after `dispose()` throws `FleetDisposedError`; `at(i)` out of
  `[0, capacity)` throws a `RangeError`; a `bind` that is not a function or does
  not return a constructor throws a `TypeError`. Construction is ATOMIC: any
  mid-prefill throw disposes the already-built members and destroys the registry
  before rethrowing. `dispose()` disposes every member LIVE AND PARKED (park ->
  dispose lands DISPOSED), then destroys the fleet-owned registry -- parked
  members are disposed too, not leaked. `null` is not zero at any gate. The demo's
  hand-rolled pool is the extracted spec (its diff went net-negative when the
  helper replaced it).
- `enableLabels(on)` / `labelOf(idOrHandle, registry?) -> string | undefined` --
  opt-in devtools labels (default OFF); per-registry `nodeId -> "Class.prop" /
  "Class#method" / "Class@anchor"`.
- `auditReactive(on)` -- opt-in leak auditor (default OFF); a lazy
  `FinalizationRegistry` reports any instance GC'd without `disposeReactive`.
- `ReactiveDisposedError` -- `extends Error`, `name` `"ReactiveDisposedError"`,
  fields `className` and `key`.
- `VERSION` -- `"1.5.0"`.

## Registry law (one registry per host chain)

`@reactiveHost({ registry })` (and `defineReactive` `host: { registry }`) binds
the WHOLE host chain to a `Registry` from lite-signal `createRegistry()`. Every
engine call the package makes -- `signalBox`, `computedBox`, `effect`,
`createRoot`, `getOwner`, `runWithOwner`, `dispose`, `nodeId`, `isTracking`,
`batch`, `untrack` -- routes through that bound registry. The `registry` value is
duck-checked for all 11 methods; a `RegistryConfig` (or a partial facade) is a
named throw naming the first missing method. A subclass may repeat the SAME
registry object or omit it (inherits the ancestor's); passing a DIFFERENT
registry down a chain is a named throw. This closes the cross-registry dispose
trap: lite-signal's default `dispose` is a silent no-op across registries, so a
custom-registry instance torn down through the default would leak -- routing
every call through the bound registry means it never does. `setDefaultRegistry`
is out of contract: the facade captures the import-time top-level helpers, so a
consumer swapping the default registry mid-life is not supported.

## Disposal law

One anchor per instance owns all deriveds and effects; signal boxes are created
bare (not adopted) and disposed explicitly. `disposeReactive` (or a `using`
block via `Symbol.dispose`) is the only lifecycle owner. Dispose is
allocation-free on the success path and idempotent. After dispose, every member
touch, `boxOf`, and `rootOf` throw `ReactiveDisposedError` naming `Class.key`.
Calling `disposeReactive(this)` from inside the instance's own `@derived`
computation throws a named error -- derived getters must be pure; dispose from an
effect, a subscription, or plain code instead. Self-dispose from inside an OWNED
`@reactiveEffect` is ALLOWED (D-4d): the current run completes, any later
decorated-member touch in the same body throws `ReactiveDisposedError`, no
re-runs follow, and conservation is exact -- the D-2f derived guard never fires
for effects. Disposing a FROZEN instance is refused up front with a named error
(D-2g): the poison swap cannot be installed on a frozen object, so a partial
half-dispose is never started (`using` over a frozen instance is covered too;
`Object.seal`/`preventExtensions` stay fine -- slots remain writable).
Construction is atomic at every capacity point (D-2h): if a signal box, the
anchor, a derived, or an effect overflows the registry mid-construction, `new`
throws the engine's `CapacityError` and every box already created is disposed --
no node leaks, on the decorator path (init-phase) and the buildless path alike.

## Buildless contract (defineReactive)

`defineReactive(Class, spec)` is for consumers without a standard-decorators
(2023-11) transpiler. The
spec normalizes (fail closed; `Reflect.ownKeys`, so symbol keys work):

- `signals`: an array of keys (each initial `undefined`) OR a map
  `{ key: value | { initial | init | equals } }`. A plain non-function,
  non-object value is the initial; a descriptor uses `initial` (verbatim) or
  `init` `(self) => value` (per instance), never both; a bare function is a named
  throw (ambiguous -- wrap it in `{ initial: fn }` or `{ init }`).
- `deriveds`: a map `{ key: (self) => value | { get, equals } }`.
- `effects`: a MAP ONLY `{ key: (self) => void | { run, scheduler } }`.
- `locals`: a MAP ONLY `{ key: { source, equals?, initial? } }` -- the buildless
  twin of `@localTo` (PD-57). `source` is REQUIRED and must be a `(self) => value`
  function (a missing or non-function source is a named throw, fail closed);
  `equals` governs the upstream compare only; `initial` (verbatim, when present)
  selects the @trackedReset flavor, its absence the @localCopy flavor. Same
  read/write laws and ABA contract as the decorator.
- `host`: `{ registry }` or omitted -- the same validation as `@reactiveHost`.

Spec-declared members that collide with an own property of `Class.prototype` are
a named throw. The class's own constructor runs BEFORE wiring, so it must not
touch spec-declared members (a prewired handle turns any such touch into a named
error) -- put initials in the spec. Post-construction behavior is in full parity
with the decorator path: values, deriveds, effect methods, disposal, poison, and
capacity accounting are identical because both front doors call the SAME wiring
core.

## Introspection & audit (S4; all cold, all opt-in)

`costOf(Factory)` measures a class's settled per-instance cost by a stats-delta
probe on its bound registry: construct, read every `@derived` once (forcing the
lazy links), snapshot, dispose, verify the floor -- run TWICE, requiring
identical deltas. An inconclusive probe (a data-dependent derived read, or a
registry mutated mid-probe) or a floor-verify failure THROWS a named error;
costOf never returns a guess. `nodes` equals P+L+D+E+1 (the R-A law); `links` is
the first-full-read count. The result is frozen and cached per class. costOf
constructs the probe instance with NO constructor arguments.

`capacityFor(inventory, { headroom } = {})` turns `[Factory, count]` pairs into a
ready `createRegistry` config `{ maxNodes, maxLinks, prealloc: "eager",
onCapacityExceeded: "throw" }`. Nodes are exact (`sum(cost.nodes x count)`);
links are `sum(cost.links x count)` scaled by `headroom` (default 1 = exact),
floored at the engine minimum of 1 so a signals-only inventory stays
constructible.
FIXED-shape deriveds provision exactly; a BRANCHY derived whose active branch
reads more members than the probe measured under-provisions and the engine throws
`CapacityError` at link formation (loud, named -- raise `headroom` for such
workloads). See decisions/0007.

Labels (`enableLabels(true)`, default OFF) register, at wiring, a per-registry
`nodeId -> label` for every node an instance creates
(`"Class.prop"` / `"Class#method"` / `"Class@anchor"`); `labelOf(idOrHandle,
registry?)` resolves them (an unknown id returns `undefined` -- a miss is not an
error); `disposeReactive` unregisters. Maps are per-registry (node ids are
per-registry). OFF adds no hot-path cost -- the accessor canon is byte-identical
to 0.3.0; labels feed a `graph()`/`toTree()` devtools walk from `rootOf(vm)`.

Audit (`auditReactive(true)`, default OFF) lazily creates one
`FinalizationRegistry` and reports (one `console.error`) any instance
garbage-collected WITHOUT `disposeReactive`, naming the class + shape. OFF: no
`FinalizationRegistry` exists, nothing is registered, wiring measures unchanged.
Reach: an instance still pinned by its own undisposed derived/effect nodes on a
long-lived registry is never collected, so audit cannot fire for it -- that
retention is what the leak/retention torture catches; audit catches instances
that reach GC without dispose (e.g. a per-scope registry dropped whole).

## Rejections (all named, all fail-closed, all at decoration/definition time)

Legacy emit, wrong decorator kind, static members, private (#) members, unknown
option keys (with a nearest-key did-you-mean), non-function `equals`/`scheduler`,
double `@reactiveHost`, an unknown host option, orphaned members (reactive
members whose class never got a host), duplicate keys (subclass redeclaration OR
two stacked package decorators on one member), an invalid host `registry`, a
heterogeneous registry chain, and every `defineReactive` spec shape error each
throw a named error.

## Peer range

Requires `@zakkster/lite-signal` `>=1.5.0 <2.0.0` (peer dependency). Uses
`signalBox`, `computedBox`, `effect`, `createRoot`, `getOwner`, `runWithOwner`,
`dispose`, `nodeId`, `isTracking`, `batch`, and `untrack` from it (all 11 also
routed per-registry via `createRegistry()`). The RANGE floor is 1.5.0 and stays
1.5.0 -- everything the runtime surface needs shipped in 1.5.0 stable. Two
forward-compat torture scenarios are feature-detected above that floor and SKIP
below it (a skip below the floor is correct; at or above it is a failure): the
`createScope` adoption scenario needs peer 1.6.0, and the engine
`[Symbol.dispose]`/`using` interop scenario needs peer 1.9.0. Neither is a
runtime requirement -- the shipped surface runs on 1.5.0.

## Scope note

1.0.0 FROZE the export surface at 16; 1.1.0 adds `releaseReactive` +
`reinitReactive` (an additive MINOR under that promise) -> 18 exports: the 13
runtime exports plus `costOf`, `capacityFor`, `enableLabels`, `labelOf`, and
`auditReactive` (all cold / opt-in; the hot accessor canon is byte-identical to
0.3.0). 1.2.0 adds `localTo` (decisions/0013 strategic track, 0014 contract) as
an additive MINOR -> 19 exports; the 1.0.0 canon (`makeGet`/`makeSet`/
`makeDerivedGet`) stays byte-identical -- @localTo ships its own accessor bodies
and pays its own measured cost. 1.3.0 adds `forEachReactive` + `snapshotOf`
(decisions/0013 ladder) as an additive MINOR -> 21 exports; `snapshotOf` is the
named in-package consumer that admits `forEachReactive` under the 0009 bar, and
the 1.0.0 canon stays byte-identical. 1.4.0 adds `costOfInstance` (decisions/0013
criterion (b); the demo is the named consumer) as an additive MINOR -> 22
exports; the 1.0.0 canon stays byte-identical. 1.5.0 adds `createFleet`
(decisions/0013 criterion (d); the demo fleet is the named consumer, its
hand-rolled pool DELETED for the helper) as an additive MINOR -> 23 exports --
the 0013 ladder CLOSES at 23; the 1.0.0 canon stays byte-identical. The semver promise from here: any change to an existing export's
signature or behavior is a MAJOR, recorded in a decision file; new exports are
minors; the hot accessor canon (`makeGet`/`makeSet`) does not move without a
major. Also present since
0.3.0: the dev-side class-reactivity benchmark (`bench/`, private, never
shipped) and the fleet-soak torture scenario; the formal kill-criteria verdicts
live in decisions/0006-kill-criteria.md. Composition recipes over this frozen
surface (the MobX-parity-by-composition matrix, the two-plane fleet, the
lite-store boundary) live in COOKBOOK.md, delivered GitHub-only and NOT in the
tarball -- read it at
https://github.com/PeshoVurtoleta/lite-signal-decorators/blob/main/COOKBOOK.md
(every code block byte-verified against a GC-gated companion; decisions/0009). Still OUT of the 1.1 surface (each a
deliberate, documented exclusion, not an oversight): private (`#`) members,
static members, and module/global signals (raw lite-signal territory).

## Pooled lifetime (1.1.0)

An instance is no longer single-lifetime. It moves on a three-state lattice --
LIVE / PARKED / DISPOSED -- driven by a two-call API. `releaseReactive(vm)` parks
a LIVE instance (cascades the anchor, disposes each box, holds ZERO engine nodes,
keeps its prebuilt wiring closures); `reinitReactive(vm, initials?)` revives a
PARKED one (rebuilds boxes + anchor + deriveds + effects through the SAME
closures, values reset). Two calls, not one: park and revive are separated in
time by the pool, and `disposeReactive`'s frozen `(vm) -> boolean` signature
cannot double as park (decisions/0011). Fail closed: every member touch on a
PARKED instance throws `ReactiveDisposedError` with a *parked* message (not
"disposed"), and `boxOf`/`rootOf` agree; a throw mid-reinit routes through
disposeCore and lands the instance DISPOSED (a failed revival is final); DISPOSED
is TERMINAL -- only a PARKED instance revives, a disposed one is gone and cannot
be pooled. park->park is idempotent (`false`); dispose-on-parked lands DISPOSED
and stays idempotent. The prebuilt closure set is built LAZILY at first
`releaseReactive`, so the construct-once/dispose-once path is byte-untouched
(0011); the amortization holds -- one closure build per reused instance,
re-registered across all N acquire/release cycles with zero new allocation. See
decisions/0010 (the spike contract, measured) and 0011 (the API shape).
